newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca shares slip as bid talk eases.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca shares slip as bid talk eases.

text.p: Shares in Zeneca slipped back on Friday amid scepticism over the latest outbreak of bid speculation that took the stock to a record high in late trading yesterday, traders said.
After hitting another record of 15.90 stg on Thursday, the shares were 11p lower at 15.76 stg in early trading.

Dealers said there was talk on Thursday that Roche of Switzerland was arranging a multi-billion dollar bank loan, reviving talk of a Zeneca bid that has enlivened the share regularly in recent months.
"Personally I think it is a complete spoof but having said that, I do think there is further rationalisation to come in the pharmaceutical industry," said one senior sales trader.
U.S. pharmaceutical giant Warner Lambert was also rumoured to be preparing a 23 stg per share offer, which would value Zeneca at over 21 billion stg.

Dealers said investors were reluctant to sell Zeneca because of the chance of a bid, so any spark of investment demand tends to force the stock sharply upwards. Though no evidence of a bid has yet materialised, the rumours have refused to die, the stock rising more than 39 percent over the past 12 months.
